Design Tokens

Colours, fonts, spacing and breakpoints shared by the »Blätter« layouts: the website (Palm, blaetter-theme), the offline archive and the status page. Generated from tokens.json by ./design build, like every other file in dist/; ./design check fails when this page is out of date. The elements built from these tokens are shown in the styleguides of the consumers: the archive's docs/design-system.html, the Patternlab styleguide of blaetter-theme and the Storybook of Palm.

1 Colours

One entry per role. The code line names the custom property the website theme uses (--palm-color-*; every colour is also written as --blaetter-color-<role>). Not part of the dark theme, used on the website only: red-light, red-dark, link-hover, link-on-dark, success, warning.

  • #FFFFFF page
    --palm-color-white
    page, sticky headings, layers, fields
  • #000000 text
    --palm-color-black
    running text, headings, titles, navigation
    dark: not pure white, which glares
  • #E51736 red
    --palm-color-red
    logo, labels, active item, arrows
    the red of the »Blätter« logo (no Pantone base); until 11/2026 the website used #E71835. Dark: the website's red-light for text (the logo red has only 3.9:1 on the dark page, text needs 4.5:1); backgrounds, frames and lines keep the logo red (3:1 is enough there)
  • #EC465D red-light
    --palm-color-red-light
    lighter red; in the archive the dark theme's red text (see red.dark)
  • #C8102E red-dark
    --palm-color-red-dark
    website: hover of red buttons (white text on it)
    darker instead of lighter on hover: white on the lighter red had only 3.8:1
  • #086D9A link
    --palm-color-blue
    links, buttons
    dark: own value (the website's blue-light #097EB2 has only 4.0:1 on the dark page); button backgrounds stay
  • #097EB2 link-hover
    --palm-color-blue-light
    website: hover of action buttons
  • #5DB4E3 link-on-dark
    --palm-color-blue-on-dark
    website: links on black or dark images (hero, poster teasers, navigation)
    the link colour of the dark theme; replaces #4AC6FF
  • #086D9A focus
    --palm-color-focus
    focus outline
    the website used #66AFE9 with a glow until 2026 (only 2.3:1 on white)
  • #6B6B6B muted
    --palm-color-muted
    grey text: meta lines, counts, sources, descriptions, quotes
    replaces #808080 as text on the website since 2026 (3.9:1 on white)
  • #808080 boundary
    --palm-color-grey-text
    borders of fields, checkboxes and light buttons only (3:1 is enough, WCAG 1.4.11); never as text
  • #CCCCCC rule-strong
    --palm-color-grey-border
    thick heading rules, layer frames
  • #E3E3E3 rule
    --palm-color-grey-dark
    row separators, cover frames
  • #F2F2F2 surface
    --palm-color-grey
    tiles, hover rows, notices, buttons
    the website's page ground (page wrapper), so grey elements become white with a frame there; see README, Grounds
  • #FFE9A0 marker
    --blaetter-color-marker
    search words, highlighted text
    own: the website's mark is #FFFF00; calmer and still 4.5:1 for links on it
  • #008000 success
    --palm-color-success
    website: success messages, checklists, valid form fields
  • #A35A00 warning
    --palm-color-warning
    website: warning messages (rule and icon)
    replaces Classy's #E09600 (2.5:1 on white); dark enough for text as well

3 Cover hues

The hues of the covers since the print layout of 2026; the palette stays over the years, the issues rotate through it. Assumed values until the designer's sRGB values for the Pantone U colours are in. Only for bars, dots and large figures (3:1 on the page); never as running text. Dark values: mixed with 20 % white.

6 Breakpoints

Three steps for all layouts. Media queries cannot read custom properties, so CSS writes these queries out literally; --blaetter-media-* documents them and serves scripts.

NameMedia queryWidthFor
phone(max-width: 45rem)up to 720 pxphones: one column, compact elements (folded filters, buttons at full width); the main step of the website's legacy styles
above-phone(min-width: 45.001rem)from 720 pxeverything that is not phone
desktop(min-width: 75rem)from 1200 pxlaptops and larger screens: wider layouts of the website's legacy styles
wide(min-width: 88.75rem)from 1420 pxthe website's page width: side columns next to the content, e.g. the filters of the search

8 Shared rules

Grounds: the website differs

The archive and the status page lie on white (page); grey (surface) marks a tile, a notice or a hover row on it. The website still lies on grey: its page wrapper is surface. An element that is grey on white elsewhere would vanish there, so on the website it turns around: white with a frame. Moving the website onto white is a later, larger step.

Archive, status page: on white

Notice: grey, rule at the left.

Website: on grey

Message: white, framed in its colour.

Rules for every layout

  • Colours, fonts, spacing and breakpoints come only from tokens.json; consumers keep verbatim copies and check them (see README). A new value starts here, never in a consumer.
  • Text reaches 4.5:1 on its ground, focus outlines and borders of controls 3:1; a new pairing gets an entry in contrast.pairs.
  • Grey text is muted; boundary is for borders of controls only, never for text.
  • Focus is always visible: a solid outline or ring in focus (3:1 on its ground), no soft glow.
  • Colour is never the only signal: a cover hue or a status colour always comes with a word, an icon or a shape.
  • Cover hues are for bars, dots and large figures, not for running text or links.
  • Spacing uses the steps of the scale, media queries the three breakpoints; the website's legacy styles move onto them when their part is rebuilt.

Generated from tokens.json. Change the tokens there, then ./design build and ./design copies --update.
